form.title: Memory Configuration
form.description: Configure enablement and extraction strategy across L0-L4 memory layers.
form.l1DependencyTitle: Raw event memory is the long-term foundation
form.l1DependencyDescription: When disabled, downstream knowledge, reflection, and strategy memory stay disabled.

enable_l0.label: Enable working context
enable_l0.description: Keep short-lived runtime state in memory and checkpoint it for crash recovery.

enable_l1.label: Enable raw event memory
enable_l1.description: Persist long-term source events that feed later cognition and retrieval.

enable_l2.label: Enable knowledge memory
enable_l2.description: Extract stable entities, relationships, and defensive ToM assertions from raw events.

enable_l3.label: Enable summary & reflection memory
enable_l3.description: Generate synthesized summaries and reflective abstractions from accumulated events.

enable_l4.label: Enable strategy & execution memory
enable_l4.description: Capture repeatable strategies and failure-avoidance heuristics from prior runs.

runtime_replay_include_l0_only.label: Replay working-context-only runtime events
runtime_replay_include_l0_only.description: Include ephemeral execution events when replaying short-term context after recovery.

enable_t1_importance.label: Enable importance scoring
enable_t1_importance.description: Score event salience before promoting items into downstream cognition.

enable_l1_vectorization.label: Enable vectorization (semantic search)
enable_l1_vectorization.description: Vectorize raw events to enable semantic similarity search.
enable_l1_vectorization.description_disabled: Requires an embedding model to be configured first.

enable_l2_llm_extraction.label: Enable LLM knowledge extraction
enable_l2_llm_extraction.description: Use the model to derive entities, relations, and ToM assertions from raw events.

enable_l3_llm_summary.label: Enable LLM reflection summary
enable_l3_llm_summary.description: Use the model to build reflective summaries from retained memory streams.

enable_l3_vectorization.label: Enable vectorization (semantic search)
enable_l3_vectorization.description: Vectorize reflection summaries to enable semantic similarity search.
enable_l3_vectorization.description_disabled: Requires an embedding model to be configured first.

enable_l4_skill_extraction.label: Enable skill extraction
enable_l4_skill_extraction.description: Promote repeated success or failure patterns into future procedural guidance.

overview.subtitle: Start with cross-layer search, overall signals, layer entry cards, and recent changes before choosing where to go deeper.
overview.searchResultsBody: Cross-layer clues for "{{query}}" are collected here first so you can quickly decide which workspace is worth opening next.
overview.searchIdleBody: Once you enter a keyword, this area gathers the relevant clues into a calmer, easier-to-read surface.
overview.searchIdleHint: No search results yet. Try a preference, person, place, or skill name, then follow the densest layer.
overview.noSearchResults: No matching memory surfaced yet. Try a more specific term, or enter a layer directly from the overview below.
overview.workspaceBody: Use this area to move into each independent memory page. Every layer keeps its own filtering model and reading rhythm so you can go deeper without losing orientation.
overview.workspaceHint: Read the signal density here first, then enter a specific layer once you know where the useful movement is.
overview.statsBody: The five memory layers now live on independent pages, making it easier to expand each workspace without flattening everything into one screen.
overview.asideTitle: The memory space feels calm today, but the signals keep growing
overview.asideBody: Start with search or a layer card, then use recent changes to decide which layer is most worth opening next.
overview.recommendedBody: When search results start leaning toward a layer, this area suggests where to go next.
overview.recommendedEmpty: There is no strong search bias yet. Start from the layer you care about most.

workbench.subtitle: Inspect runtime workbench context, active sessions, and current workbench contents.
workbench.searchPlaceholder: Filter workbench memory by session ID or status
workbench.focusBody: The workbench page is best when entered through a concrete session, then used to inspect goals, active entities, and temporary tactics together.
workbench.sessionBody: Start from the currently focused session, then decide whether you need the deeper goal stack and workbench contents below.
workbench.queueBody: This lighter rail helps you choose which runtime thread deserves attention before diving into the full workbench.

events.subtitle: Inspect the long-term event stream and filter it by content or source.
events.searchPlaceholder: Filter event memory by content, type, or domain
events.focusHeadline: Read the density of memory intake by source and content
events.focusBody: This layer behaves like a retained draft of experience. Narrow by source first, then move into the event contents.
events.sourceSummaryBody: Start by seeing which sources are still feeding the memory stream under the current filters.
events.domainSummaryBody: Event domains help you judge whether the current slice is about behavior, preference, or background context.

knowledge.subtitle: Inspect the knowledge graph, ToM assertions, and lab controls with entity-aware filtering.
knowledge.searchPlaceholder: Filter knowledge memory by entity, relation, or assertion
knowledge.focusBody: The knowledge page should feel like a slow-growing garden. Start with entity type, then move deeper into relations, assertions, and snapshots.
knowledge.entitySummaryBody: Use the active entity types to sense what kind of knowledge is surfacing before reading the full structure.
knowledge.structureBody: Frequent predicates and identity-link counts offer a quick read on the shape of the graph.
knowledge.identitySummary: {{count}} identity links in the current filtered view

reflection.subtitle: Inspect generated reflections and summaries with type-aware filtering.
reflection.searchPlaceholder: Filter reflection memory by summary content or category
reflection.focusHeadline: See how memory is being gently reorganized
reflection.focusBody: This layer is no longer raw record. It is the language that remains after time and summarization start to shape the memory.
reflection.cadenceBody: Check which summary types are active first, then move into the written reflections with that rhythm in mind.
reflection.topicsBody: This keeps the repeated themes visible so you can feel the direction of the reflection layer at a glance.
reflection.noTopics: No explicit topics surfaced in the current summaries

skills.categoryBody: Start with the most active categories, then move into specific capabilities when you know where the concentration is.
skills.attentionBody: This area highlights stable capability and any state that may still need a closer look.
